Every dot is a day someone bought Eli Lilly stock, 8,637 of them from 1972 to 2006. Red means that buyer is losing money.

One day later: 47% are red.
Ten years: still 2,423 red.

At 19 years and 7 months, not one dot is losing.

The last red dot bought in November 1998 and was red for over nineteen and a half years. Today it's one of the biggest stocks on the planet.

Every single person who waited made money.

Split-adjusted price, dividends excluded.
